findings.title: Overwrite guard is placed on a function `sq review code` does not call
findings.description:
T12 adds the archive-and-verify guard to `save_review_file` only. The unmet success criteria are "Re-running `sq review code <N>` over an edited review file archives the prior content and warns" and the F003 fail-closed criterion.

- **CLI path:** every review command calls `save_review_result` (`src/squadron/cli/commands/review.py:451`, `:523`, `:610`, `:746`), which writes with its own `path.write_text(...)` at `persistence.py:300` and `:303`. It never goes through `save_review_file`.
- **Pipeline path:** when `slice_info` is present it also uses `save_review_result` (`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review.py:255`). `save_review_file` is reached only in the no-`slice_info` fallback (`:272`).
- **Tests:** T13 exercises `save_review_file` directly, so all three tests would pass while the walkthrough's step 7 still silently destroys the hand note.

Fix: T12 should put the guard in one shared write helper used by both `save_review_file` and `save_review_result` (markdown and `as_json` branches). T13 should add a test that re-saves through `save_review_result`.

Two smaller gaps in the same task:
- `save_review_result` returns `Path`, not `Path | None`, so the "return `None` on abort" contract needs an explicit decision for that caller.
- The design's "review content is still printed to the terminal" on abort has no task step.

findings.title: Relocation leaves `review/addressed/` importing from the pipeline package
findings.description:
T3 tells the implementer to keep `verification.py`'s `RoundDiff` import from `pipeline.actions.findings_addressed.screens` after the move, calling it "the pipeline→review direction". Once the file lives in `review/addressed/`, that import is review→pipeline. That is the inversion the design's "Dependency direction (review F002)" paragraph exists to prevent.

- **Same problem in T5:** `judge_residue_core` takes a `diff` typed `RoundDiff` (`findings_addressed/judge.py:21`, `:94`), so `review/addressed/judge.py` would need the same back-import. T5 does not mention it.
- **Likely import failure:** importing `squadron.review.addressed.verification` first would trigger `findings_addressed/__init__.py`, which imports back from the still-initialising `review.addressed.verification`. File 2's `review/resolution.py` and the CLI would import in that order.
- **Why the verify tasks would miss it:** T2/T4/T6/T8 enter through the pipeline package first, so the cycle is not exercised.

Fix: move the `RoundDiff` dataclass (`screens.py:34`) into `review/addressed/models.py` in T1, leaving `compute_round_diff` and the screens in the pipeline. Add one check to a verify task: import `squadron.review.addressed` in a fresh interpreter and assert it pulls in no `squadron.pipeline` module.

findings.title: T6 demands "no test rewritten" but T5 moves the mocked transport
findings.description:
Both judge suites patch `squadron.pipeline.actions.findings_addressed.judge.run_review_with_profile` (also `tests/pipeline/test_findings_addressed_e2e.py:27`). After T5 the call lives in `review/addressed/judge.py`, so that patch target must change or the mock no longer intercepts the call. T6 says any test edit means "stop and reconcile with the design", so a correct extraction halts the implementer.

T7 has the same tension. All four test files import through the package `__init__` (e.g. `tests/pipeline/test_findings_addressed.py:18`), and T7 removes those re-exports without shims.

Fix: state in T5–T7 that import paths and patch-target strings are the permitted edits (the design allows "import-path updates"), and that assertions and fixtures must not change. T1's "expected importers" list should say the test files are updated at T7, not T1.

findings.title: cf-scanning check (T14) is sequenced after the Part D commit
findings.description:
The design's Phase 5 note requires the cf `archive/` check "sequenced before Part D lands". T14 is numbered after T12/T13, and T13 carries the `fix:` commit, so the archive filename scheme is committed before the go/no-go is known. The task file patches this with "do not mark T12 done until T14" in two places, which a sequential executor will hit too late.

Fix: move T14 ahead of T12 and delete the two cross-referencing caveats.

T14's first source, `ai-project-guide/tool-guides/context-forge/`, is also absent from this checkout: a glob of `project-documents/ai-project-guide/tool-guides/` returned nothing. The task should name a source that exists, or state its `BLOCKED:` condition directly.

findings.title: `reviewedSha` "both paths" criterion is only half-tested, and T10 is ambiguous
findings.description:
The success criterion requires the stamp "from both the CLI and the pipeline persistence paths". T11's integration test covers "`save_review_result` (or the pipeline review action, whichever is more directly testable)", which is one path.

The pipeline action has two branches: `save_review_result` (`:255`) and a direct `format_review_markdown` call (`:265`). A stamp resolved inside `save_review_result` covers the first automatically; the second needs its own wiring and its own test. T10 does not distinguish them.

T10 also writes `run_git(..., cwd=...)` for `save_review_result`, which has no `cwd` parameter (`persistence.py:257-267`). The task should say where the working directory comes from.

Fix: resolve HEAD in one helper, name both pipeline branches in T10, and make T11 assert the stamp on the no-`slice_info` branch as well.

findings.title: Part 0 is over-split for a mechanical move
findings.description:
Eight tasks and four commits cover a relocation the design calls mechanical. T2, T4, T6 and T8 only re-run the existing suite.

- Merge T1+T3 (move models, parsing, verification) with one verify step and one commit.
- Keep T5+T6 (the extraction is the only real change).
- Fold T7's export and docstring edits into T5/T6, with T8's full-suite run as the closing step.

That gives roughly three tasks and two commits. Across both files, 40 tasks for a 3/5 slice is heavy; file 2's wiring-only pairs (T27/T28 for example) are candidates for the same merge.

findings.title: File 2 leaves two success-criteria details untested
findings.description:
These are outside this file but affect slice coverage.

- T26 tests a judge transport that raises, but not an "unreadable judge response" (parse failure), which the F004 criterion names separately.
- T32 tests metrology's `discover_judge_results` only. The criterion also says "review discovery" returns no resolution artifacts, and T17's own `{index}-review.*.md` glob deserves the same assertion.

findings.title: Commit markers are plain lines but not in the `**Commit**:` form
findings.description: Markers are written as `- Commit:` sub-bullets. They are correctly not checkboxes and sit after test tasks, but tooling that looks for `**Commit**:` will not see them.

findings.title: Test-with ordering and traceability for Parts 0/A/D
findings.description: Every implementation task is followed directly by its test or verify task, and every task traces to a design part (F002 relocation, Decision 1, Decision 7/F003). There is no scope creep. No NFR is restated in the slice, so no load-test or CI-gating task is required. File 2 depends on file 1 with no circular dependency.
